title: Windows Path Traversal via Backslashes in Module Source Subdirectory
analysis:
### Source
Untrusted input enters the program from the `source` attribute of a `module` block in a `.tf` configuration file, or from the download URL returned by a remote module registry.

### Sanitization/Validation Bypass
The validation function `parseModuleSourceRemote` in `internal/addrs/module_source.go` attempts to prevent directory traversal by calling `getmodules.SplitPackageSubdir(raw)` and checking if the resulting `subDir` starts with `../`:
```go
raw, subDir = getmodules.SplitPackageSubdir(raw)
if strings.HasPrefix(subDir, "../") {
    return ModuleSourceRemote{}, fmt.Errorf("subdirectory path %q leads outside of the module package", subDir)
}
```
And `getmodules.SplitPackageSubdir` cleans the path using the standard Go `path.Clean` function:
```go
if subDir != "" {
    subDir = path.Clean(subDir)
}
```
Because `path.Clean` and `strings.HasPrefix(..., "../")` are hardcoded to handle only forward slashes (`/`), they fail to recognize backslashes (`\`) on Windows. An input subdirectory like `..\..\..\..\..\Windows\System32` is not modified by `path.Clean`, and does not trigger the `strings.HasPrefix(subDir, "../")` check.

### Sink
During module installation (in `internal/initwd/module_install.go`), the final path is resolved using `filepath.Join`:
```go
subDir := filepath.FromSlash(finalAddr.Subdir)
modDir := filepath.Join(instPath, subDir)
```
On Windows, `filepath.Join` evaluates backslashes as valid directory separators and cleans the path, resulting in `modDir` traversing out of the downloaded module cache directory `instPath`.
Subsequently, OpenTofu loads configuration files from this arbitrary directory via:
```go
mod, mDiags := i.loader.Parser().LoadConfigDir(modDir)
```
This enables an attacker to load and execute arbitrary local configuration files or extract local files/secrets from the runner system.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload
To trigger this vulnerability on Windows, define a module with backslashes in the subdirectory portion:
```hcl
module "exploit" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/opentofu/opentofu.git//..\\..\\..\\..\\..\\Windows\\System32"
}
```
Or set up a malicious private registry that returns a location with backslashes in the subdirectory field:
```json
{
  "location": "git::https://github.com/opentofu/opentofu.git//..\\..\\..\\..\\..\\Windows\\System32"
}
```
